# Sync records between tools for backups

**Pattern:** Two-System Sync · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers backups work end to end across HubSpot, Slack, Airtable and Discord.

It moves through 15 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Hourly Schedule
2. Map to Canonical Schema
3. Route by Event Kind
4. Handle 'created' → HubSpot
5. Handle 'updated' → HubSpot
6. Handle 'deleted' → HubSpot
7. Log Unrecognized Kind
8. Consolidate Handling
9. Align Field Names
10. Cap Batch Volume
11. Guard Non-Empty sourceId
12. Save Execution Metadata
13. Summarize Run Stats
14. Append Audit Row (Airtable)
15. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Discord — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing backups work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Hourly Schedule → Map to Canonical Schema → Route by Event Kind → Handle 'created' → HubSpot → Handle 'updated' → HubSpot → Handle 'deleted' → HubSpot → Log Unrecognized Kind → Consolidate Handling → Align Field Names → Cap Batch Volume → Guard Non-Empty sourceId → Save Execution Metadata → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Airtable) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Discord

## Use it for

- Teams keeping HubSpot and Slack aligned by hand for backups
- Backups work where "Map to Canonical Schema" is still a manual step before HubSpot
- Backups work that only reaches HubSpot on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps HubSpot and Slack in step for backups, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed HubSpot or Slack call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 17 nodes in this backups build
- Branches rejoin before HubSpot, so a backups run reports once rather than 17 times
- Every backups run leaves an audit row behind, alongside HubSpot
- Fans the same result out to Airtable in the same run, for backups

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Airtable PAT; Discord webhook URL; HubSpot private-app token; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The optional HMAC check runs before any business logic touches the payload — bad signatures are rejected at the door rather than after work has already been done with untrusted data. Acking fast (HTTP 202) and doing the real work after the response is what stops the sender's webhook delivery from timing out and re-delivering the same event.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Turn on signature verification and trace what a tampered payload does at the 'Signature Valid?' gate.
2. Add a new event kind to the switch and give it its own handler.
3. Remove the fast-ack step and observe how response time changes under a slow downstream write.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**HubSpot private-app token**
HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Grant the CRM scopes you need; legacy API keys are deprecated and will not work.

**Airtable PAT**
airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.
_Gotcha:_ Scope the token to the specific base, and grant `data.records:write`. Field names are case-sensitive.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy URL.
_Gotcha:_ Webhook mode needs no bot token. Messages cap at 2000 characters.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your backups process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- HubSpot: a private-app token carrying only the CRM scopes these nodes use — legacy API keys are deprecated and over-broad.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Airtable: scope the PAT to this one base and to `data.records:write`; a token scoped to the workspace can rewrite every base.
- Discord: give the bot access to the destination channel only, not the whole guild.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole backups payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
